title: Maximal Rectangle
interviewTips: Clarify input type: List[List[str]] of '0'/'1' vs char[][] vs int[][], and empty matrix handling.
Trade-off: brute force O(m^2 n^2) vs histogram+stack O(m*n) time O(n) space vs DP boundaries O(m*n) time O(n) space without stack; mention reuse of Largest Rectangle in Histogram (Problem 84).
Edge-case tip: single row or column reduces to longest consecutive ones; all zeros returns 0; update heights to 0 on '0' and use sentinel 0 to flush monotonic stack.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Enumeration
approaches.intuition: Fix top-left corner at every '1' and expand downward row by row, tracking minimum width of consecutive ones so far. Area of rectangle from top row i to current bottom row k is minWidth * height.
approaches.theory: For each start cell (i,j) that is '1', iterate bottom row k >= i. For each k compute width of ones starting at j in row k. If width is 0 the rectangle cannot extend further down, break. Otherwise minWidth = min over rows i..k, candidate area = minWidth * (k-i+1). Take global max. Correct because any maximal rectangle has a top edge and its width is limited by narrowest row.

timeComplexity.explanation: mn start cells, up to m bottom rows each, each width scan up to n. Worst O(m^2 n^2), with m rows n cols. Slightly tighter O(m^2 n^2) bound; optimized variant caching row widths is O(m^2 n).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only a few integer variables besides input.

steps: start (1,2): k=1 width=3 minWidth=3 area=3, k=2 width=3 minWidth=3 area=6 -> max=6
start (1,3): k=1 width=2 area=2, k=2 width=2 area=4
start (2,0): k=2 width=5 area=5, k=3 width=1 minWidth=1 area=2
no larger rectangle found, answer stays 6

edgeCases: empty matrix or empty row returns 0
all zeros returns 0, all ones m*n returns m*n
single row reduces to max consecutive ones

approaches.name: Approach 2: Histogram + Monotonic Stack
approaches.intuition: Build histogram per row where heights[j] is number of consecutive ones ending at current row. Each row then asks for largest rectangle in histogram, solved with increasing stack.
approaches.theory: If matrix[i][j]=='1' then heights[j]+=1 else heights[j]=0. Any rectangle with bottom edge at row i corresponds to a histogram rectangle with height limited by min heights over its columns. Largest Rectangle in Histogram is solved in O(n) with monotonic increasing stack storing indices: when current height < stack top height, pop and compute width = i - newTop -1. Doing this for all m rows gives global optimum in O(m*n).

timeComplexity.explanation: Each row updates n heights O(n) and histogram scan is amortized O(n) since each index pushed and popped at most once. Total O(m*n).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Heights array size n plus monotonic stack up to n.

edgeCases: column of zeros keeps heights zero
sentinel 0 flushes remaining stack to handle non-decreasing tail
use strictly less comparison to correctly handle equal heights

approaches.name: Approach 3: DP with Height Left Right Boundaries
approaches.intuition: Maintain for each column height of ones plus leftmost and rightmost boundaries of rectangle that can extend to current row. Area per column is (right-left)*height.
approaches.theory: height[j] counts consecutive ones ending at row i. left[j] is max left boundary seen so far constrained by zeros, updated with cur_left. right[j] is min right boundary constrained by zeros, updated with cur_right scanning right to left. For row i, feasible width for column j is right[j]-left[j]. Max over j gives best rectangle ending at row i. This is O(m*n) without explicit stack.

timeComplexity.explanation: Three linear passes per row over n columns: update height+left, update right, compute areas.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Three arrays height, left, right each size n.

steps: areas: col0=3, col1=5, col2=3, col3=6, col4=6 -> max 6
row3 zeros reset height[1]=0 height[2]=0 and shrink boundaries

edgeCases: must reset right[j]=n on zero else stale boundary leaks
must take max of left and min of right across rows to enforce all-rows constraint
single column works: left=0 right=1 height=count
